column3: “His” is supplied before father and mother.
The historical present becomes past; “a man” and “his wife” supply the participants.
“Jesus” makes the subject explicit; the historical present becomes past.
“Live like eunuchs” interprets making themselves eunuchs.
“Jesus” makes the pronoun explicit; “for them” and “those who brought them” specify the recipients of prayer and rebuke.
The historical present becomes past; “the man” supplies the subject.
“To follow” makes following the purpose of leaving.
“Of all things” is supplied to renewal.
BSB includes “wife” with the Textus Receptus (γυναῖκα); the critical text lacks it.
